title: Manage Mantic configs and expected expenses
summary: Initialize one private database and create, read, edit, or delete named configs and their fixed expense recurrence rules. Preserve current definitions only.
use_when: The caller wants to initialize Mantic state or create, read, edit, rename, or delete its calculation configs and expense items.
do_not_use_when: The caller wants to record payments, save a balance or forecast run, share an item among configs, or integrate directly with SQLite.
outcome: Mantic returns selected current definitions or atomically applies an authorized definition change in the selected single database.
effects: Initialization can create private directories and empty schema-one state. Edits atomically change current definitions. Config deletion also deletes its owned items.
Agent command dispatch can separately append metadata-only Chancery usage.
authority: Mantic validates definitions and owns committed configuration state. The caller supplies expense meaning and authorizes edits.
success: A successful read returns complete selected current definitions. A successful write reports the resulting definition or deletion after commit.
failure_and_recovery: Invalid input or a failed transaction preserves prior definitions. Missing or unsupported state stops ordinary commands; initialize empty state explicitly or select a compatible program.
After interruption, inspect current definitions before repeating a create or add. No write idempotency key or retained revision exists.
privacy: Private state retains config names, item labels, amounts, schedules, and schema metadata. Config history, balances, runs, payment state, and generated occurrences are not retained.
does_not_authorize: Changing another product, sharing private output, modifying SQLite directly, or replacing populated state.

interfaces.label: Add an expense item
interfaces.invocation: /Users/joey/.local/bin/mantic item add CONFIG NAME AMOUNT --first DATE [--every UNIT [--interval N]] [--end DATE]

interfaces.label: Update an expense item
interfaces.invocation: /Users/joey/.local/bin/mantic item update ID [--name NAME] [--amount AMOUNT] [--first DATE] [--every UNIT] [--interval N] [--end DATE | --clear-end] [--once]

consumers.statement: Local users and authorized agents manage reusable calculation definitions through Mantic's CLI.

preconditions.statement: Ordinary commands require initialized supported state; init accepts empty or supported schema-one state. Config names are unique, case-sensitive, trimmed, nonempty, and free of controls.

inputs.statement: Commands select one invocation-wide database and accept config names or item IDs, positive integer-cent expense amounts, a first due date, optional day/week/month/year recurrence and positive interval, and an optional inclusive cutoff.

outputs.statement: Reads return complete selected current definitions. Writes report resulting records or deletion. --json uses schema-one success result envelopes on stdout and coded operation errors on stderr.

data_semantics.statement: config holds only ID and name; config_item holds ID, exclusive config reference, label, amount_cents, first_due, nullable paired recurrence unit/interval, and nullable end_date. Definitions are current editable state without revisions.

identity_and_units.statement: Config and item integer IDs are local to the selected database. Config names select configs. Item names are nonunique labels. All monetary values use integer cents in one caller-chosen currency with two decimal places; dates are calendar dates.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Lists and show cover all committed selected configs or items at their read boundary. No stored revision, current-balance timestamp, run timestamp, or active-config selection exists.

access.statement: The supported boundary is the local CLI and current-user filesystem permissions. Default state is ~/Library/Application Support/Mantic/mantic.db; --database requires an absolute invocation-wide path.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Each validated change commits atomically. Config deletion cascades to owned items. Unspecified update fields retain their values. Forecasts never advance stored schedule anchors.

operational_limits.statement: Amounts fit signed 64-bit cents, expenses are positive, recurrence intervals are 1 through 4,294,967,295, and dates range from 0001-01-01 through 9999-12-31. SQLite contention uses a five-second busy timeout without a hard wall-clock objective.
No database-capacity, read-latency, write-latency, or future migration-window objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Initial state and CLI output schemas are independently one. Unsupported or foreign state fails; ordinary commands do not initialize, migrate, or repair it.

reliances.statement: Agent CLI dispatch attempts metadata-only command usage through Chancery's Rust journal API; missing attribution and internal calls are skipped, and recording failures preserve Mantic results.
